title: Netanel's Gift
summary: Netanel, leader of the tribe of Issachar, worries that his gift for the Mishkan is exactly the same as the gift of the leader who came before him. With his daughter's help, he discovers that what makes a gift special is the heart that gives it. The story ends with the Priestly Blessing.
pages:
The new Mishkan, the Tabernacle, stands in the middle of the camp. It is so shiny and beautiful.
And Netanel, leader of the tribe of Issachar, wants to bring it a gift.

"I have an idea!" Netanel tells all the leaders.
"Let's bring wagons and oxen to help carry the Mishkan when we travel."
And that's what they did.

God tells Moses: each leader will bring another gift, each on his own day.
One day, one leader.
Twelve days of celebration!

On the first day comes Nachshon, leader of the tribe of Judah.
He brings a big silver plate, a silver bowl,
and a small golden spoon full of sweet-smelling incense.

Tomorrow is Netanel's turn. But that night he can't fall asleep.
"Oh," he whispers, "my gift is exactly like Nachshon's. The same plate, the same bowl, the same spoon. So what's special about it?"

His daughter, Naama, snuggles up beside him.
"Abba, when I draw you a picture, and my brother draws you a picture too, is it the same picture?"

"Not at all," says Netanel. "Every picture is special, because each of you drew it just for me."
Naama smiles. "Then your gift is special too, Abba."

In the morning Netanel brings his gift.
He holds the golden spoon carefully, and smiles.
His whole heart is inside this gift.

And so, day after day, all the leaders come.
The very same gift, twelve times over.
And each time it is new, because each one gives it in his own way.

Then Aaron the priest and his sons raise their hands and bless all the people:
"May the Lord bless you and keep you. May the Lord make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you. May the Lord lift up His face toward you and give you peace."

Naama closes her eyes.
The blessing wraps around her like a soft, warm blanket.

You can give a gift from the heart too: a drawing, a hug, a kind word.
And when Abba and Imma bless you on Friday night, it's exactly the same blessing, and every time, it's yours.
